title: Cabe destacar que: señalar un dato importante

sections.content: Cabe destacar que (it's worth noting that, notably) flags a fact the writer wants the reader to pay special attention to -- common in academic and historical writing to highlight something significant within a broader narrative. It's an impersonal construction: cabe doesn't change for person or number. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Cabe destacar que, en 1980, Adolfo Pérez Esquivel recibió el Premio Nobel de la Paz por su trabajo en defensa de los derechos humanos.
items.english: It's worth noting that, in 1980, Adolfo Pérez Esquivel received the Nobel Peace Prize for his human rights work.

items.spanish: Cabe destacar que buena parte de esta resistencia dependió también de redes internacionales de solidaridad.
items.english: It's worth noting that much of this resistance also depended on international solidarity networks.

items.spanish: Cabe destacar que la Vicaría de la Solidaridad fue fundada directamente por la Iglesia católica, no por un partido político.
items.english: It's worth noting that the Vicariate of Solidarity was founded directly by the Catholic Church, not by a political party.

items.spanish: Cabe destacar que estos movimientos guerrilleros fueron, en general, minoritarios dentro del conjunto de la resistencia.
items.english: It's worth noting that these guerrilla movements were, in general, a minority within the resistance as a whole.

sections.content: Cabe destacar que is a fixed impersonal phrase, like hay que -- never conjugate destacar to agree with the fact being highlighted (never cabe destacan que, even with a plural subject afterward).
